  SyncMos: Scalable Motion Synchronisation for Multi-Agent Scene Interaction

    Text-guided motion generation in 3D scenes has ad-                coordination, where actions such as handing, receiving, or

vision, machine learning, and embodied AI. Recent ad-

2. Related Work
                                                                        Figure 1. Overall architecture. The framework first interprets
2.1. Human motion synthesis                                             the user’s input via a high-level planner, and low-level controller
                                                                        synchronizes the timing of each-character.
Recent advances in human motion synthesis stem from im-
provements in dataset fidelity [14, 23] and the emergence of
diffusion-based generative models [17, 21]. These models
synthesise realistic motion from various inputs, including              constraint-based editing. Recent deep learning models in-
action labels [7], text [17], and 3D scene context [1, 16].             troduce spatial conditioning for motion synthesis [10], yet
Beyond single-agent motion, recent work extends to hu-                  temporal control remains more challenging since shifting
man–human [12] and human–scene interactions [9]. In-                    one action requires globally consistent adjustment across
terGen [12] produces realistic two-person interactions but              frames. InterGen [12] learns two-character interactions
relies on fixed-size joint modelling, limiting scalability to           without explicit timing control but still struggles to produce
larger groups or dynamic agent counts. LINGO [9] enables                synchronised or temporally diverse behaviours. Our frame-
autoregressive motion synthesis in structured 3D scenes,                work addresses this limitation through diffusion-based tem-
generating long-horizon human–scene interactions. How-                  poral control using Diffusion Posterior Sampling (DPS) [6]
ever, existing single-agent models, including LINGO, lack               on a pre-trained single-character motion model.
mechanisms for temporally aligned multi-agent coordina-
tion. In contrast, our work introduces SyncMos, a gen-
eral framework that combines an LLM-based dependency-
                                                                        3. Overview
aware event planner with a diffusion-based synchronisation
module, achieving scalable and temporally coherent multi-
                                                                        Figure 1 illustrates the overall architecture of SyncMos,
agent interaction without retraining.
                                                                        a scalable framework for temporally synchronised multi-
2.2. LLM-based Scene-level Agent Planning                               agent motion generation from free-form textual instruc-
                                                                        tions. The framework consists of two main components: a
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong                   high-level event planner and a low-level motion synchro-
capabilities in reasoning, planning, and few-shot learn-                nisation module.
ing [15, 18]. Recent works have leveraged LLMs for
scene-level human action planning. Digital Life Project                    The high-level event planner analyses the user’s textual
(DLP) [3] constructs autonomous virtual humans with                     instruction using a large language model to extract struc-
lifelike social behaviours, but its focus is on simulat-                tured event descriptions with temporal and causal depen-
ing digital life rather than generating coordinated mo-                 dencies. It also integrates 3D scene context, such as object
tions. Sitcom-Crafter [5] introduces a plot-driven frame-               segmentation, spatial relations, and scene geometry to gen-
work that integrates diverse interactions within 3D environ-            erate an ordered sequence of actions across multiple agents.
ments, though it remains limited to two-character scenar-               The resulting plan specifies which actions each agent per-
ios. Event-Driven Storytelling [13] decomposes complex                  forms and the corresponding temporal schedule.
narratives into sequential events for scalable multi-character             The low-level motion synchronisation module synthe-
behaviour generation in 3D scenes, yet lacks explicit tem-              sises detailed motion sequences for each agent using a
poral dependency modelling and precise synchronisation                  single-agent diffusion-based generative model conditioned
across agents. In contrast, our framework models both                   on the planned events. To ensure temporal consistency
sequential and parallel event dependencies and achieves                 across agents, this module incorporates a time-warping
cross-agent synchronisation through time-warping control.               mechanism and Diffusion Posterior Sampling (DPS) [6] to
                                                                        align motion timing and interaction phases. Through this
2.3. Temporal Motion Synchronisation                                    two-level architecture, SyncMos extends single-agent mo-
Precise temporal coordination is essential for generating               tion generation frameworks to coordinated multi-agent sce-
natural and coherent motion. Classical methods such as                  narios without retraining, providing a scalable and mod-
motion warping [20] and Laplacian optimisation [11] ad-                 ular approach for generating temporally synchronised hu-
just timing in captured sequences through interpolation and             man–scene interactions.

Experiment Setup We evaluate the planner on a custom                    nisation model using a controlled timing adjustment experi-
benchmark of 30 multi-character narratives spanning three               ment focused on object-grasping motions. This experiment
scene types, House, Office, and Restaurant with two to five             corresponds to the most challenging dependency scenarios
agents per scenario. Two example scenes are visualized in               described in Sec. 6.1, where precise temporal alignment is
Fig. 6. The benchmark comprises two subsets: Synchro-                   essential for coordinated multi-agent actions.
nisation (15 scenarios) testing parallel multi-agent actions,
and Dependency (15 scenarios) testing long-horizon causal
chains. Each scenario includes a ground-truth event graph               Experiment Setup Scene data from the LINGO dataset
G = (E, R) with annotated sequential and parallel rela-                 are used to construct 15 distinct test cases, each beginning
tions. We compare against the Event-Driven Storytelling                 from a shared initial pose and targeting objects at different
baseline [13], which autoregressively generates events with-            spatial locations. The reference grasp timing is defined as
out explicit global dependency modelling. Planner back-                 the frame when the wrist joint first reaches within a distance
bones include GPT-4o and Qwen-3 (235B/8B). We report                    threshold of the target object.

7. Conclusion                                                                             These backbone-specific artifacts are independent of our
                                                                                          synchronisation mechanism, and we expect SyncMos
We introduced SyncMos, a framework for generating tem-                                    to benefit directly from future advances in single-agent
porally synchronized multi-agent motion using a single-                                   diffusion-based motion generators. While the framework
agent diffusion model and an LLM-based dependency-                                        is model-agnostic, extending the evaluation to additional
aware planner. The planner extracts structured event se-                                  motion models is an important next step. Future work
quences with sequential and parallel relations, and the pro-                              also includes incorporating physics- or contact-aware
posed temporal synchronisation module aligns cross-agent                                  constraints, enabling tighter feedback between planning
timing through time-warping and diffusion-based refine-                                   and generation, and expanding the system to more diverse
ment. Experiments on multi-agent scenarios demonstrate                                    or interactive settings.
that SyncMos can enforce temporal dependencies and pro-
duce coordinated behaviors without requiring multi-agent
model training.                                                                           Impact and value SyncMos introduces a novel formula-
                                                                                          tion for synchronised multi-agent motion generation by co-
Limitation and futurework Although SyncMos                                                ordinating multiple agents without requiring a multi-agent
achieves consistent temporal alignment, several limitations                               model. By combining single-agent generation with plan-
remain. Large timing adjustments may reduce refinement                                    ning and temporal refinement, the method reduces model
stability, and LLM-based planning can introduce errors                                    complexity and offers practical utility across applications.
in long or ambiguous narratives. The current synchro-                                     We expect SyncMos to provide a useful basis for future
nisation module performs time-warping within a fixed                                      work on scalable scene-level interactions.
motion duration and cannot modify the overall motion
length. Extending the method to support temporal scaling                                  8. Acknowledgements
of the motion itself remains an interesting direction for
